summary: Design: stem (shaft, collar, setting pinion G, crown) + loose winding pinion on the stem + spring-loaded sliding sawtooth clutch sleeve (on_stem) + crown_wheel (contrate rack-pin ring, 20 pins, + 12T spur) + 30T gear and 20-tooth sawtooth ratchet on the barrel arbor + spring click + setting_wheel (contrate ring + 12T spur meshing the minute wheel). Checked with my own manifold3d overlap script: rest overlaps (none above 0.0002 except the supplied minute_post/dial_plate pair, 0.034 mm3), the AT-0 held tests (all above 0.03 mm3), and case bounds. Rough kinematic sweeps (overlap-clearing, no friction/force model): winding train gives about 5.1 crown turns per arbor turn without jamming; setting train moves the minute wheel about 14.5 degrees per 90 degrees of crown in both directions without jamming; clutch teeth lift the clutch over ramps backward and the click clears forward and holds against backward by geometry (about 1 degree slack). The real rig's friction/force model, the AT-2 hold, the pull/push stops (including intermediate stops) and the full AT-1..AT-6 sequences were NOT simulated, so I claim not_tested for them.
